description.narrative:
Increased access to finance for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), especially micro and small enterprises (MSEs): IFC expects this investment will enhance financing for MSMEs, particularly micro and small enterprises in Bhutan. MSEs or Cottage and Small Industries (CSIs) are the backbone of the Bhutanese economy. CSIs constitute 95% of the total industries/enterprises in the country and employ over 100,000 people (12% of population), including women and the vulnerable section of society. CSIs play a major role in supporting economic growth and balancing regional development.
Beyond the project level outcomes, IFC anticipates that the Project will increase competitiveness in Bhutans MSME, finance market, particularly for the Bhutanese CSI industry, thus helping address the countrys access to finance gap. Therefore, through this Project, IFCs support to a large lender with wide and deep market penetration will promote increased competitiveness in the MSE sector by demonstrating lender confidence in the MSE segment and the viability of scaling up lending to this segment.

The proposed investment entails a senior, unsecured debt investment of up to US$20 million equivalent in Bank of Bhutan (BOB or the Bank) under Bhutans revised External Commercial Borrowing (ECB) guidelines. The loan is structured as a Bhutanese Ngultrum (BTN) linked, fixed rate, amortizing loan with tenor of upto 5 years. The IFC loan proceeds will be utilized by BOB to grow and expand their micro and small enterprise (MSE) loan portfolio. Subject to BFC approval, the Project will be included in the FIG MSME Platform which is supported by a pooled first loss guarantee (PFLG) of up to US$40 million provided by International Development Association (IDA) 20 Private Sector Window Blended Finance Facility (IDA-PSW BFF) allocated to the SME Envelope under the MSME Finance Platform, as well as IDA-PSW Local Currency Facility (LCF) in the form of cross-currency swap.
